precepts.text: Was returning, and sitting in his chariot read Esaias the prophet. Then the Spirit said unto Philip, Go near, and join thyself to this chariot. And Philip ran thither to him, and heard him read the prophet Esaias, and said, Understandest thou what thou readest? Because we will study, we will get certain instructions, but is there a follow-up to those instructions? Sometimes we give an instruction, and do we follow up and say, did you understand what I am telling you to do? Or do you go, boy, I said do it, do it. That kid is now intimidated, afraid to do it. Are we giving the proper instructions and seeing if the person is actually ascertaining the instructions that they are given? Are they just repeating what they are seeing, trying to make it? Because you know, black people, we will buy something that has to be put together and we will dump all the pieces out, we will separate them and look at the box and put the pieces together like we see it on the box, instead of reading the instructions. Well, that is what we do with the scriptures. We will read, we will study. But are we really challenging ourselves on what is being studied? Are we asking the questions? Are we going back to say, hey, I am reading this but I do not understand any of that? And as leaders, are we giving the instructions to the people? And he said, How can I, except some man should guide me? We all have to be guided in the instruction that we are getting. You cannot just tell a person to go do something. We are all instructed until it becomes habit.
precepts.point: The soul of the sluggard desireth, and hath nothing: but the soul of the diligent shall be made fat. This is the society that we have created. A bunch of sluggard men. They have not been instructed on what hard work is. And even yourself, how many books can you say that you have read and completed in your lifetime as an adult? And then to take it a step further, how many books have you read outside of the Bible and completed as an adult? Now put that on the kid. Are you challenging them to create a habit of starting something and finishing it?

note.label: From Broken Men Comes Ungodly Generations

precepts.why:
“A wise son heareth his father’s instruction”. When you first come in as a brother, you are still attached to the life you are coming out of; somebody has to instruct you. Acts shows it. The eunuch “Was returning, and sitting in his chariot read Esaias the prophet. Then the Spirit said unto Philip, Go near, and join thyself to this chariot. And Philip ran thither to him, and heard him read the prophet Esaias, and said, Understandest thou what thou readest?”

We study and we get certain instructions, but is there a follow-up? When we give an instruction, do we follow up and ask, did you understand what I'm telling you to do? Or is it, boy, I said do it, do it, until the kid is intimidated and afraid to do it? Are we checking whether the person is actually ascertaining the instructions, or just repeating what they see and trying to make it?

Black people will buy something that has to be put together, dump all the pieces out, look at the picture on the box and put it together like that instead of reading the instructions. That is what we do with the scriptures. We read and study, but are we challenging ourselves on what we study? Are we asking the questions and going back to say, I'm reading this, but I don't understand any of it? And as leaders, are we giving the instructions to the people?

“And he said, How can I, except some man should guide me? And he desired Philip that he would come up and sit with him.” We all have to be guided in the instruction we are getting. You can't just tell a person to go do something. We are all instructed until it becomes habit, and that is how a son learns to hear his father's instruction instead of becoming the scorner who hears not rebuke.

precepts.text: Philip heard the eunuch read the prophet Esaias and said, understandest thou what thou readest? And he said, how can I, except some man should guide me? You get people that say just read on your own, you do not need anybody. Stop listening to them.
precepts.point: As ye have been taught: some of the leadership from the old school went off, and the doctrine became that everything they taught was wrong, so throw it away and go back to Christianity. Men make mistakes, men do fall, but when they were in their prime they were teaching properly. You do not throw the baby away with the bath water.

note.label: Deceived by Enticing Words: Colossians 2

precepts.why:
Colossians says, “Rooted and built up in him, and stablished in the faith, as ye have been taught.” We must be rooted in Christ, and to be rooted you have to be studying; and if you are studying, you had better be applying, because you will be tested. A brother tells another brother to do what the scriptures say, and that brother gets mad and leaves because he is being pressured to do God’s work. That is simple.

“As ye have been taught”: the faith comes by being taught. Acts shows it: “And Philip ran thither to him, and heard him read the prophet Esaias, and said, Understandest thou what thou readest? And he said, How can I, except some man should guide me? And he desired Philip that he would come up and sit with him.”

The eunuch was reading the prophet Isaiah and could not understand it without a man to guide him. There are people who say, just read on your own, you do not need anybody. Stop listening to them. Being established in the faith comes by being taught, as the eunuch was taught by Philip.

At that time there was a great persecution against the church at Jerusalem, and they were all scattered abroad throughout Judea and Samaria, except the apostles. Notice that unlike the other epistles, the book of Acts never closes with Amen, showing there is a continuation: the apostles come back on the scene and redo the Acts all over again, so the things that happened back then are the things that happen today.

There will be a great persecution today. This gospel is a witness against the whole world. When you pray thy kingdom come, thy will be done, you are saying the Most High's will overpowers America's will, Russia's, China's, every nation racing for world domination. To preach a black Christ in the streets is to speak against the system that was designed to keep our people debased, a Christ with many crowns upon his head who takes the crowns of all the nations. They are not going to let a people they despise rise up and preach a gospel that overthrows the world superpowers and do nothing; it is going to be a great persecution. Gird your mind, study, pray, and apply, because wisdom and knowledge will be the stability of our time.

note.label: Acts 8: The Word Scattered Abroad, and the Baptism unto the Conscience

points: Devout men carried Stephen to his burial and made great lamentation over him. A devout man is a man according to the laws of the Most High who has a good report.

note.label: Acts 8: The Word Scattered Abroad, and the Baptism unto the Conscience

points: As for Saul, he made havoc of the church, entering into every house, haling men and women and committing them to prison. This is the same spirit that will rise up in the religious leaders again; they will seek after us and put us through hell, thinking they do the Most High a service.

Because of this you have to be as a pilgrim, one that is ready to get up at any moment and abandon everything. They may come to your house to arrest you, and you have to be ready to leave the pretty house, the picket fence, and the comfortable bed at the drop of a dime, the way our fathers were fugitives. Christ warned the disciples this would happen from city to city, and it came to pass, and it is coming again.

note.label: Acts 8: The Word Scattered Abroad, and the Baptism unto the Conscience

points: Therefore they that were scattered abroad went every where preaching the word. Because of the great persecution the disciples had to flee, and our fathers were fugitives, always on the run, the way it was done to men like Nat Turner. It is going to come to that point again, where a brother might have to house a teacher whose name is on the news, wanted for sedition; you might be charged as guilty by association, but you have to see past it to protect your brother, because the gospel has to go forward. This is why we need such a high level of unity and love for one another to survive.

note.label: Acts 8: The Word Scattered Abroad, and the Baptism unto the Conscience

points: Then Philip went down to the city of Samaria and preached Christ unto them. Philip was preaching to the Jews who lived in Samaria, not yet to the Gentiles; the Most High moves in order, causing interruptions and persecutions to push his chess pieces and further spread the gospel.

note.label: Acts 8: The Word Scattered Abroad, and the Baptism unto the Conscience

points: The people with one accord gave heed to the things Philip spoke, hearing and seeing the miracles he did. Unclean spirits, crying with a loud voice, came out of many that were possessed, and many taken with palsies and that were lame were healed, and there was great joy in that city.

note.label: Acts 8: The Word Scattered Abroad, and the Baptism unto the Conscience

points: Before this there was a certain man called Simon who used sorcery and bewitched the people of Samaria, giving out that himself was some great one, and they all gave heed, from the least to the greatest, saying, This man is the great power of God. History outside the Bible says Simon Magus followed Peter performing tricks, became known as the father of heretics, taught salvation by grace alone without works, and finally fell to his death when Peter commanded the demons carrying him to release him; the validity of that account is uncertain, but it shows Simon was a sorcerer deceiving the people.

Christianity works the same way, a binding spell over our people that covers the eyes from seeing the truth. You can read the plain scripture that Christ is black and that he came first to the lost sheep of the house of Israel, and they walk away not believing, or say they do not want to hear the Bible, only your opinion, and then reject that too. It is an enchantment to the highest level, where a man can read something in front of them and they see something else.

note.label: Acts 8: The Word Scattered Abroad, and the Baptism unto the Conscience

points: But when they believed Philip preaching the things concerning the kingdom of the Most High and the name of Jesus Christ, they were baptized, both men and women. Then Simon himself believed also, and was baptized, and continued with Philip, wondering at the miracles and signs. Some of our brothers recover themselves, though the outside history says Simon never truly recovered and went back to what he was doing.

note.label: Acts 8: The Word Scattered Abroad, and the Baptism unto the Conscience

points: When the apostles at Jerusalem heard that Samaria had received the word of the Most High, they sent Peter and John, who prayed for them that they might receive the Holy Ghost. Notice the order: Philip, the deacon, woke up the city and planted, but the apostles had to come and put the spirit on them. It is the same order today, where the bishop and the apostles visit the cities where new schools open and pray over the congregation.

note.label: Acts 8: The Word Scattered Abroad, and the Baptism unto the Conscience

points: As yet the Holy Ghost was fallen upon none of them; only they were baptized in the name of the Lord Jesus. They first had to believe in Christ in the place of animal sacrifice, believing that Christ could forgive sins when Moses' sacrifices could not. The subject matter of that day was the law and animal sacrifice versus the name of Jesus Christ, which is why the apostles keep saying to repent and believe in his name.

note.label: Acts 8: The Word Scattered Abroad, and the Baptism unto the Conscience

points: Then the apostles laid their hands on them and they received the Holy Ghost, after they had repented and believed in Christ. There are two different baptisms: John's water baptism, which came from the Levitical purification laws and was symbolic of repentance, and Christ's baptism with the Holy Ghost, which is the laws and the cleansing of the conscience. Water can only wash the dirt off the skin; it cannot clean the evil in your mind. Christ magnified the law within the conscience, showing that sin starts in the mind, so his cleansing purifies your consciousness through his word.

note.label: Acts 8: The Word Scattered Abroad, and the Baptism unto the Conscience

points: When Simon saw that through laying on of the apostles' hands the Holy Ghost was given, he offered them money, saying, Give me also this power, that on whomsoever I lay hands he may receive the Holy Ghost. Simon had the spirits of covetousness, envy, preeminence, and vainglory; he had held status as the great power of God, and when he lost it those spirits rose up in him and he wanted to buy back what he had, thinking, I have the money, I will pay you for what you have.

note.label: Acts 8: The Word Scattered Abroad, and the Baptism unto the Conscience

points: Peter said, Thy money perish with thee, because thou hast thought that the gift of the Most High may be purchased with money; thou hast neither part nor lot in this matter, for thy heart is not right. Repent therefore of this thy wickedness and pray, for I perceive thou art in the gall of bitterness and in the bond of iniquity.

This is why, when people come into the truth, some who had status, fame, or money as celebrities, pastors, or deacons have to come up as a member and clean themselves. Some get jealous, hold on to the envy, and try to bring different doctrines to sway members away, the same spirit of bitterness that moved the Pharisees to kill Christ because the disciples came from nowhere, spoke more eloquently, and went to the scriptures better without the status.

note.label: Acts 8: The Word Scattered Abroad, and the Baptism unto the Conscience

points: The gall of bitterness is resentment and bitterness of spirit. Simon became jealous because the signs the Most High worked through the apostles overshadowed what the people had known him for. That thing did not come overnight; he fed envy, preeminence, vainglory, and covetousness day by day until the roots of bitterness took hold and bound him, and he became a prisoner of his own mind, trapped and sinning.

note.label: Acts 8: The Word Scattered Abroad, and the Baptism unto the Conscience

points: Then Simon answered, Pray ye to the Lord for me, that none of these things which ye have spoken come upon me. And when they had testified and preached the word of the Lord, they returned to Jerusalem and preached the gospel in many villages of the Samaritans.

note.label: Acts 8: The Word Scattered Abroad, and the Baptism unto the Conscience

points: The angel of the Lord told Philip, Arise, and go toward the south unto the way that goeth down from Jerusalem unto Gaza, which is desert. And he arose and went, and behold, a man of Ethiopia, an eunuch of great authority under Candace queen of the Ethiopians, who had charge of all her treasure and had come to Jerusalem to worship.

People say this proves Philip went to the heathen Ethiopians, but this eunuch was a Jew, part of the remnant of Israel scattered in Ethiopia, in Kush, during the Babylonian and Persian captivity. That is why Christians confuse the Ethiopian eunuch; they do not understand Bible prophecy or Bible history. Candace was a real title of the queens of the kingdom of Kush who ruled from the city of Meroe, and the queen of that time was likely Amanitore, around the same period as the famine in Acts chapter 11.

note.label: Acts 8: The Word Scattered Abroad, and the Baptism unto the Conscience

points: The eunuch was returning, sitting in his chariot, reading Esaias the prophet, and the Spirit said to Philip, Go near and join thyself to this chariot. Philip ran and heard him read Isaiah and asked, Understandest thou what thou readest? The eunuch answered, How can I, except some man should guide me, and desired Philip to come up and sit with him.

note.label: Acts 8: The Word Scattered Abroad, and the Baptism unto the Conscience

points: The place of the scripture he read was Isaiah: He was led as a sheep to the slaughter, and like a lamb dumb before his shearer, so opened he not his mouth; in his humiliation his judgment was taken away, and who shall declare his generation, for his life is taken from the earth.

note.label: Acts 8: The Word Scattered Abroad, and the Baptism unto the Conscience

points: The eunuch asked Philip, Of whom speaketh the prophet this, of himself or of some other man? He did not know, so rather than assume or give his own interpretation, he asked. That is how you should handle what you do not know: write it down and ask, rather than making an assumption and teaching others, which is how heresies come into the body. Then Philip opened his mouth, began at the same scripture, and preached unto him Jesus, because Philip had the Holy Ghost, wisdom, and understanding, having learned under the feet of the apostles.

note.label: Acts 8: The Word Scattered Abroad, and the Baptism unto the Conscience

points: As they went on their way they came to a certain water, and the eunuch said, See, here is water, what doth hinder me to be baptized? Philip said, If thou believest with all thine heart, thou mayest. He answered, I believe that Jesus Christ is the Son of God, and he commanded the chariot to stand still, and they went down both into the water, and Philip baptized him.

This seems to contradict everything taught earlier about Christ's baptism not being water. Philip baptized the eunuch in water because, like Ezra and others, some of the disciples came from John the Baptist's teaching and held to his water baptism; John understood his own place and told his disciples to follow Christ, who must increase while he decreased.

note.label: Acts 8: The Word Scattered Abroad, and the Baptism unto the Conscience

points: When they came up out of the water, the Spirit of the Lord caught away Philip, that the eunuch saw him no more, and he went on his way rejoicing. But Philip was found at Azotus, and passing through he preached in all the cities till he came to Caesarea.
